newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Police pursue killers of Cambodian PM's relative.
newsitem.headline: Police pursue killers of Cambodian PM's relative.

text.p: Police have launched a full-scale investigation into the killing of Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen's brother-in-law, officials said on Wednesday.
Em Sam An, secretary of state for the Interior Ministry, told Reuters no suspects had been identified yet, but police were actively pursuing the case.
Keov Samuth, 39, was gunned down outside a Phnom Penh restaurant on Tuesday morning by two assailants, who fled on a motorbike.
A funeral for Keov Samuth, who was married to Hun Sen's wife's sister and was employed as a senior Interior Ministry police official, was scheduled for Thursday.

A tearful Hun Sen said on Tuesday that the killing was meant as a warning to 10 Khmer Rouge separatists who had spoken out against a leading opposition party and Hun Sen's coalition partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
At a press conference on Wednesday, one of the separatists told reporters the men, who said they had been undercover Khmer Rouge agents, feared for their lives.
"Of course, we are afraid of threats to our lives," said Sieng Sophearak, who was flanked by two other separatists and several bodyguards.

Sieng Sophearak, who called himself a special envoy of Hun Sen, repeated previous allegations that opposition leader and former finance minister Sam Rainsy had taken secret funds and support from the Khmer Rouge, and had cooperated with the pariah Maoist movement to discredit the government.
Ranariddh has called the men liars and Sam Rainsy has said he has been slandered.

In comments that analysts said were likely to exacerbate political tensions between the co-premiers, Sieng Sophearak also suggested that Ranariddh's royalist FUNINPEC party was far weaker than Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
"If there were no CPP, the Khmer Rouge would be able to take over the country in one year," he told reporters.
Political tensions within the coalition government have flared over the separatists' claims.
